import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_2/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_2/test_1.csv"
    ]

    # Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)

    # Both sources have the exact same schema as the target schema.
    # According to Hint 2, since schemas are identical, UNION (concat) is preferred.

    # Check columns are exactly the same and in the same order
    expected_columns = [
        'tripduration', 'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station id', 'start station name',
        'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station id', 'end station name',
        'end station latitude', 'end station longitude', 'bikeid', 'usertype', 'birth year', 'gender'
    ]

    # Reorder columns if needed (defensive)
    df0 = df0[expected_columns]
    df1 = df1[expected_columns]

    # Concatenate the two dataframes (union)
    df_union = pd.concat([df0, df1], ignore_index=True)

    # Ensure data types match target schema exactly:
    # Target schema types:
    # 'tripduration': int
    # 'starttime': string
    # 'stoptime': string
    # 'start station id': int
    # 'start station name': string
    # 'start station latitude': float
    # 'start station longitude': float
    # 'end station id': int
    # 'end station name': string
    # 'end station latitude': float
    # 'end station longitude': float
    # 'bikeid': int
    # 'usertype': string
    # 'birth year': int
    # 'gender': int

    # Convert columns to target types carefully, handling missing or malformed data:
    # For integer columns, convert with errors='coerce' then fillna or convert to int safely.

    int_columns = [
        'tripduration', 'start station id', 'end station id', 'bikeid', 'birth year', 'gender'
    ]
    float_columns = [
        'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station latitude', 'end station longitude'
    ]
    str_columns = [
        'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station name', 'end station name', 'usertype'
    ]

    # Convert integer columns
    for col in int_columns:
        # Coerce errors to NaN, then convert to Int64 (nullable integer dtype) to preserve NaNs if any
        df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    # Convert float columns
    for col in float_columns:
        df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

    # Convert string columns
    for col in str_columns:
        df_union[col] = df_union[col].astype(str)

    # After type conversion, if any integer columns have NaNs, decide how to handle:
    # Since target examples have no missing values shown, we can fill NaNs with a default or drop rows.
    # Here, we will drop rows with any NaNs in integer columns to keep data clean.
    df_union = df_union.dropna(subset=int_columns)

    # Reset index after dropping rows
    df_union = df_union.reset_index(drop=True)

    # Save the final dataframe to the target CSV path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_2/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    df_union.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
